clue.text: A kiss in love story said to make a neat ending

indicators.note: the kiss sits in the middle of the love-plus-story combination, so in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter O

indicators.note: said tells the solver the story word is only heard, its spelling being swapped for one that sounds the same

parts.note: a story is a tale
a kiss is written as a cross, the letter X, at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A romantic tale with a kiss in it is told so as to round things off nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is an old word for cattle, so a neat ending is the tail of an ox; oxtail is a British soup and stew meat. 'said' turns TALE into TAIL, and 'in' puts X inside O + TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic term for cattle or an ox, and the end of an ox is its tail, sold as a cut of beef.

clue.text: Charge too much?

parts.note: reads like overcharging a customer, but means putting too great an electrical or physical burden on something

explanation.definitionFit: To charge something too heavily, with cargo or current, is to burden it beyond its capacity.

clue.text: To surpass score is excellent

parts.note: to surpass a rival is to top them
to score a mark on wood is to cut a notch

explanation.surface: Beating a total of twenty points counts as an excellent result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like twenty or a points tally; here it is a cut mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal phrase for first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: In a way, it means this month

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: A remark explaining, in some fashion, that a word refers to the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' (short for instant) is old business-letter English for the current month, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.'
explanation.definitionFit: Inst. abbreviates instant, a formal commercial term for the present calendar month.

clue.text: Light equipment for miner and motorist

definitions.text: Light equipment for miner and motorist

parts.words: Light equipment for miner and motorist
parts.note: a lamp worn on a miner's helmet and the main front light on a car share one name

explanation.definitionFit: Both a miner's helmet lamp and a car's front beam are lights mounted at the head of the wearer or vehicle.

clue.text: Won't want to, particularly if remarks are in bad taste!

definitions.text: Won't want to, particularly if remarks are in bad taste!

parts.words: Won't want to, particularly if remarks are in bad taste!
parts.note: pictures someone reluctant to retract what they said, joking that tasteless remarks would be unpleasant to swallow

explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement humiliatingly is idiomatically to swallow what you said, here made literal with remarks that taste bad.

clue.text: Spot the wimp

definitions.meaning: a single drop of liquid, as a leaking tap lets fall

explanation.definitionFit: A drop of water is one sense; a weak, spineless person is the slang sense.

clue.text: Following inflation it offers comfort to the holidaymaker

definitions.text: Following inflation it offers comfort to the holidaymaker

parts.words: Following inflation it offers comfort to the holidaymaker
parts.note: inflation sounds like rising prices, but here it is pumping up an inflatable mattress used on holiday

explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress becomes a comfortable place to sleep for campers once blown up.

clue.text: Party leader's contempt for the platform

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from the word party

parts.note: odium means hatred or contempt

explanation.surface: A political party's chief shows disdain for the manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'platform' suggests a party manifesto, fitting the political surface; it is a raised stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a small raised stand for a speaker or conductor, a kind of stage.

clue.text: Unveil the ultimate sex-op surgery

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the final letter of the word the is used
surgery cuts and rearranges, so the letters of sex-op are reworked

explanation.surface: Disclose all about the final sex-change operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose something is to uncover it, removing what hid it from view.

clue.text: Bar on a flight

parts.note: suggests a drinks bar aboard an aircraft, but means a metal rod holding carpet on a flight of steps

explanation.definitionFit: A rod fitted across each step holds a carpet runner in place on a staircase.

clue.text: Hears pianola transcription for wind instruments

indicators.note: transcription is rewriting music for other instruments, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A listener hears a player-piano piece rearranged for woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: These are stringed boxes sounded by the wind blowing across them, named after Aeolus, the Greek god of winds.
explanation.definitionFit: These harps are played by the breeze itself, so they are literally instruments sounded by wind.

clue.text: Spoil the sound of an instrument

indicators.note: the sound of tells the solver to take how a word is pronounced rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Ruin the tone produced by some musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' looks like a verb, ruin; it is the noun, plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are goods taken by force or theft, which is plunder or booty.

clue.text: A flower possibly open before the end of July

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of open might be rearranged into another order
the end of a word is its final letter, taken from July

explanation.surface: A bloom might open before July is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The peony is a garden plant with large showy blooms, flowering in early summer.

clue.text: A state of pure chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters of pure are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A condition of total disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' reads as a condition; it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American country, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Improve on a repair

parts.note: to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Do better than a patched-up fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to correct it and make it better.

clue.text: Cattle, it's said, may be gathered

indicators.note: it's said marks a word spoken rather than seen, so a same-sounding spelling is entered

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: Livestock may be rounded up, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' suggests rounding up cattle; it means learned, as in 'I gathered you were away'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gathered news is to have learned of it by report, much as having been told.

clue.text: Performed with a high degree of skill

definitions.meaning: carried out or completed, as a task achieved

definitions.text: with a high degree of skill

explanation.definitionFit: A task brought to completion has been achieved; a gifted musician is expert in that sense.

clue.text: A doubter disposed to be stubborn

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of a doubter are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A sceptic is inclined to be obstinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed to be' reads as 'inclined to be' in the surface; 'disposed' is the anagram signal and 'to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An obdurate person refuses to change their mind, which is obstinate.

clue.text: Not paying attention in Leeds, she crashed

indicators.note: crashed suggests wreckage, so the letters of Leeds and she are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A careless woman had a car accident in Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless, taking no notice of warnings.

clue.text: Not good value for a bun, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of value for a bun are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bread roll that sadly isn't worth the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfavourable means adverse or poor, the opposite of promising.

clue.text: Number of mischievous characters in digs

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
elves are impish little folk of folklore

explanation.surface: Some sprites live in student lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like the British word for rented rooms; it is the verb, researches or excavates.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig or search deeply into something.

clue.text: Rob irregular corporal of horse

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters of Rob are rearranged

parts.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer, abbreviated NCO

explanation.surface: Rob, an unruly cavalry corporal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporal of horse' is a real cavalry rank, which hides that 'horse' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is a wild or half-tamed horse of the American West.

clue.text: Get money for working in near chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters of near are scrambled

explanation.surface: Earning a living while things nearly fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to be paid wages in return for labour.

clue.text: Dishonest, and wary about publicity

definitions.meaning: keen to stay out of the light, hidden

explanation.surface: Crooked, and anxious to avoid the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A shifty dealer is untrustworthy; a place out of the sun is in shade, hence away from the glare of attention.

clue.text: Pool giving pleasure to many

parts.note: fun means enjoyment or pleasure
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, standing for many

explanation.surface: A swimming pool that delights lots of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like a swimming pool; it is a shared sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of money collected for a purpose is a kitty or reserve.

clue.text: Barely deserved

definitions.meaning: fair, merited, as in a fitting punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Only just covers the narrow-margin sense; a fair or merited reward is the other.

clue.text: Land that lies around in the water?

definitions.text: Land that lies around in the water?

indicators.note: around suggests turning things about, so the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about ground that sits encircled by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue both describes a small piece of land surrounded by sea and rearranges 'lies'.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Vehicle needs protection for the front

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
a guard gives protection

explanation.surface: A van needs armour to be sent up to the battle line.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the leading part of an army or movement.

clue.text: English country property

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A rural house in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions owned by a person.

clue.text: Caledonian will be put out by this cost

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of this cost are disrupted

explanation.surface: A Scot will be annoyed at the price.
explanation.walkthrough: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland; 'put out' plays on the stereotype of the thrifty Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonian means of Scotland, from its Roman name.

clue.text: Quiet place for a school break

definitions.meaning: a playtime or holiday between lessons

explanation.surface: Somewhere peaceful for pupils' playtime.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove set back in a wall is one sense; a pause in lessons or sittings is the other.
